inventory.visualPurpose: The two-block Acetylcholine receptors text (book 235, top half) — the nicotinic and muscarinic receptor definitions with their subtype/distribution lists
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: PURE TEXT, TWO BLOCKS (pdfimages: zero raster images; VLM census attempt returned 401 twice in subagent context, so the census stands on pdfimages + the text layer): the NICOTINIC block — 'Nicotinic ACh receptors are ligand-gated channels allowing efflux of K+ and influx of Na+ and in some cases Ca2+. Two subtypes: NN (found in autonomic ganglia, adrenal medulla) and NM (found in neuromuscular junction of skeletal muscle).' — followed by the MUSCARINIC block — 'Muscarinic ACh receptors are G-protein–coupled receptors that usually act through 2nd messengers. 5 subtypes: M1–5 found in heart, smooth muscle, brain, exocrine glands, and on sweat glands (cholinergic sympathetic).' No figures, margin notes, or mnemonics print in the ACh half.
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual (AchReceptorMap in visuals/pharm-p10.tsx — the ACh dispatcher chip, the nicotinic channel glyph with K+ efflux / Na+ and in-some-cases Ca2+ influx arrows plus the NN and NM subtype chips, the muscarinic GPCR glyph with its G-protein → 2nd-messenger cascade plus the five M1–5 location chips with the cholinergic-sympathetic sweat exception, the exam-targets band, and the one-key-three-locks banner); the two printed blocks are also carried verbatim in the note's table block (blocks[1]), core.what, and recall[0-1]
